articleSummary: In Xi'an, China, tick-borne disease Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie Bandavirus, has entered its spring-active period as temperatures rise. Since April 1, 2026, SFTS is classified as a Category B infectious disease in China. Incubation is 1–2 weeks after tick bite; early signs include fever ≥38°C and thrombocytopenia, with fatigue, headache, myalgia, nausea, diarrhea, and lymphadenopathy. Without timely treatment, severe cases may progress to skin bruising, bleeding, altered consciousness, and multi-organ failure, with a high death risk. There is no specific antiviral therapy or vaccine; prevention is essential. Transmission occurs mainly via tick bites, but direct contact with infected blood or secretions, or contact with virus-carrying livestock/pets, poses additional risk. High-risk groups: farmers, outdoor workers, campers, and pet owners; outbreaks peak March–July, with autumn rebounds in some areas.

articleSummary: China’s CDC sentinel surveillance shows the nationwide influenza virus positive rate rising for three consecutive weeks, with northern provinces reporting higher positivity than the south. The surge is driven mainly by Influenza B activity, following a two-year gap in B-dominant peaks as population immunity wanes and recent temperature fluctuations worsen transmission. High-risk groups include the elderly, children, pregnant women, and people with chronic diseases. Symptoms for influenza B resemble influenza A: fever, cough, sore throat, myalgias; vomiting and diarrhea are more common in children. Public should wear masks, practice hand hygiene, seek prompt medical care, and avoid work or school when ill.

articleSummary: Totally Optimized PCR (Top) TB assay, an ultrasensitive molecular test, detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA in samples negative by standard cultures, enabling earlier TB identification. Jones-Lopez), the Top TB assay was reported in Nature Communications after three six-year studies analyzing 297 respiratory samples from patients at Boston Medical Center and St. Elizabeth's Medical Center. A potential link to acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease patients is noted, necessitating further study.

Early symptoms may resemble flu, but abrupt high fever, severe headache, vomiting, lethargy, neck stiffness, altered consciousness, and petechial rash require urgent medical evaluation. Prevention is vaccination-based, covering serogroups A, B, C, Y, W; full immunization is advised, along with public health measures like surveillance and rapid case investigation.

articleSummary: Minas Gerais’ SES-MG released the first 2026 LIRAa (Rapid Infestation Index for Aedes aegypti) survey, guiding control of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. articleSummary: CMNV (covert mortality nodavirus), previously seen in shrimps, fish, and other marine life, is now linked to human viral uveitis with markedly elevated intraocular pressure in cases from China. Patients presented with eye inflammation and vision issues; routine diagnostics were negative for common ocular viruses. Eye tissues contained viral particles and genetic analysis showed near-identical sequences to marine CMNV, and laboratory studies reproduced infection with similar ocular hypertension in animals, supporting causality. Transmission appears associated with exposure to raw seafood; frequent consumption of sushi or sashimi or working with seafood without protection were reported. While most cases are in China, CMNV has been detected in dozens of marine species across Europe, the Americas, and Antarctica, indicating broader global risk. Experts differ on outbreak magnitude; precautionary guidance emphasizes avoiding contact with raw seafood without protection and adequate thermal processing to reduce risk.

articleHeadline: Risk of Guillain-Barre Syndrome Rises After Dengue Infection
articleSummary: Dengue infection markedly raises Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) risk in Brazil. In a self-controlled case-series (2023–2024), dengue increased GBS incidence 1–42 days after symptom onset, with the highest risk in the first 2 weeks and returning to baseline by day 43. The incidence rate ratio was 16.75 (95% CI 10.97–25.55). Attributable risk equated to 35.5 excess GBS cases per million laboratory-confirmed dengue infections (95% CI 34.3–36.3). Of 5,055 GBS hospitalizations, 147 had documented dengue, with 89 within the 1–42 day risk window. Brazil registered >6 million dengue cases in 2024; the Americas reported 13 million dengue cases and 8,200 deaths, while the U.S. had >3,500 dengue cases in 2024. Clinicians should suspect GBS in progressive weakness during/after dengue and initiate immunotherapy (IVIG or plasmapheresis) promptly. Findings support dengue vaccination programs and highlight risks linked to arboviruses such as Zika and chikungunya.
notes: 記事サマリーはブラジルでのデング熱とGBS関連性の研究結果を中心に述べており、アメリカの症例数言及やスペイン（カナリア諸島）での発生地域指定はあるが、主題はブラジルのデング熱流行とGBS関連性。デング感染後1-42日間でGBS発症リスクが著しく上昇（IRR 16.75）することが報告されており、臨床的に重要な知見。ただしCanary Islands、Playa de las Américasなどの地理的参照はスペインであり対象国ではないため除外。

articleSummary: Dengue in Brazil is linked to Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS). In 2023–2024, Brazil recorded about 6.5 million probable dengue cases and over 5,800 deaths; by late 2025, around 1.6 million probable cases, with transmission remaining high, and Fiocruz projects about 2 million cases in 2026. A national study using SUS data (hospitalizations, dengue notifications, deaths) identified over 5,000 GBS hospitalizations in 2023–2024, with 89 following dengue infection. A case-autocontrol analysis found dengue raises GBS risk 17-fold in weeks 1–6 after symptom onset, peaking at ~30-fold in weeks 1–2; about 36 per 1 million dengue cases may develop GBS. GBS is a rare autoimmune attack on peripheral nerves causing weakness and possible paralysis. Early treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin or plasmapheresis improves outcomes; care is provided through SUS and 136 rehabilitation centers. Prevention emphasizes Aedes aegypti control, Wolbachia releases, and expanded dengue vaccination.

articleSummary: Showerheads can harbor biofilms that trap pathogenic microbes, including Legionella pneumophila, molds, and non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), with Mycobacterium avium complex detected most often. In warm, dark, moist conditions, these bacteria may be released during showers and enter the body by inhalation or skin contact. In healthy adults, NTM exposure can cause chronic mild pulmonary infection with fatigue and a persistent dry cough; risk and severity are higher for bronchiectasis patients, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals; disseminated infection is possible. NTMs are conditional pathogens, so illness is less common in normal immunity but health risks exist. Cleaning guidance: every 3 months, detach the showerhead and soak in a diluted disinfectant or 1:1 white vinegar for at least 3 hours to remove scale and biofilm; brush surfaces, rinse, and reassemble. articleSummary: Persistent SARS-CoV-2 spike protein detected in gut tissue, especially colon, in Long COVID patients vs healthy controls. articleSummary: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease (HFMD) is surging in Vietnam, with more than 25,000 cases reported in nearly three months as of April 16, 2026. The Tropical Disease Center at Hanoi's National Pediatric Hospital reports most inpatients at stage 2a with mild neurological involvement; common symptoms include skin lesions and mucosal ulcers on the mouth, palms, soles, and buttocks, while neurological complications can appear around days 2–5 (up to day 7). Enteroviruses, including EV71, are circulating. In Hanoi, a 2-year-old improved after several days of treatment, and a Lao Cai family traveled to Hanoi for care. Daily HFMD admissions average about 20; doctors treat 10–12 patients each, nurses 12–14. Weather authorities predict prolonged heat, potentially extending transmission and increasing the risk of summer infections such as Japanese encephalitis. Emphasis on hand hygiene and surface disinfection; follow-up is advised if fever persists, lethargy, rapid breathing, or neurological signs emerge.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Nodavirus: the marine virus that can cause blindness in humans - Notiulti
articleHeadline: Nodavirus: el virus marino que puede causar ceguera en humanos - Notiulti
articleSummary: CMNV, a nodavirus affecting Litopenaeus vannamei, is linked to a human ocular disease: anterior viral hypertensive uveitis (POH-VAU). POH-VAU has appeared since 2019; CMNV association identified in 2026. The syndrome features recurrent anterior uveitis with aqueous cells and precipitates and extreme ocular hypertension, with persistent high IOP causing iris atrophy, corneal endothelium loss, and irreversible optic neuropathy. CMNV’s host range includes fishes, sea cucumbers, and crustaceans across seven phyla. Its genome has two positive-sense RNA segments: RNA1 (B2 and methyltransferase-replication) and RNA2 (capsid). A Nature study found CMNV in ocular tissues with seroconversion in 70 POH-VAU patients; transmission links to exposure to aquatic animals, especially raw consumption or unprotected processing (71.4%). Experimental data show CMNV can infect mammalian cells and raise IOP in mice. China has reported CMNV-driven shrimp aquaculture losses since 2009, before discovery in 2014.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza is now recorded at 1 billion cases annually worldwide.
articleHeadline: Influenza Kini Tercatat 1 Miliar Kasus Tiap Tahunnya di Seluruh Dunia
articleSummary: Global influenza burden: WHO 2025 reports about 1 billion infections annually, with 3–5 million severe cases worldwide; Indonesia's BPOM ensures vaccines meet safety and efficacy standards, aiming for rapid, science-based registration to improve access. Vaccination substantially reduces hospitalization risk from influenza complications by 40–60%, especially for high-risk groups such as elderly, pregnant women, children, and people with chronic diseases. Transmission via respiratory droplets and contact with contaminated objects; symptoms include sudden fever, dry cough, headache, myalgia, and fatigue. Most healthy individuals recover with supportive care; antivirals may be considered for severe or high-risk cases. Influenza viruses are Orthomyxoviridae family; types A, B, C, D; A is more prevalent and pandemic-potential; B causes 15–30% of seasonal cases with lower pandemic risk. WHO-recommended quadrivalent vaccines cover four strains (two A: H1N1, H3N2; two B lineages). SH variant aligns with WHO 2024; NH for 2025–2026.

articleHeadlineTranslated: ECMO intervention saves the patient's life in septic shock with multi-organ failure in critical condition
articleHeadline: Can thiệp ECMO, giành lại sự sống cho người bệnh sốc nhiễm khuẩn, suy đa tạng nguy kịch
articleSummary: At the National Lung Hospital in Hanoi, Vietnam, a 53-year-old man (N.D.T) presented with rapid deterioration from pulmonary tuberculosis, diabetes, septic shock, pneumonia, and multi-organ failure. He required immediate ICU care, endotracheal intubation, and then extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) with continuous renal replacement therapy. Blood and lung samples were collected and analyzed with FilmArray PCR; within 4 hours Escherichia coli was detected in both lung and blood, enabling rapid initiation of targeted antibiotics while continuing anti-tuberculosis therapy. After more than five days of intensive care, he showed clinical improvement. An early tracheostomy on day 7 aided ventilation weaning. By April 6, he was fully weaned from mechanical ventilation to oxygen via tracheostomy, and by April 10 the cannula was removed with spontaneous breathing restored. Family support and a coordinated treatment strategy were highlighted as crucial to the favorable outcome.
